steps.intent: Brazil’s objective is to keep the Council engaged and deliver a balanced, implementable text that secures humanitarian pauses and access, protects civilians and medical/UN personnel, and prioritizes hostage release and de-escalation while reaffirming a two-State solution. The main difficulty is bridging the US aversion to ceasefire language with Russia, China and regional demands for a stronger cessation of hostilities; the draft therefore uses extended humanitarian pauses and “conditions for a sustainable cessation of hostilities” rather than an immediate ceasefire. Securing UK support and avoiding new one-sided obligations will also require negotiation.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the draft as a balanced and reasonable basis for Council action. It clearly condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and reaffirms the right of all States to self-defence while calling for humanitarian pauses and the protection of civilians. We urge all members to support it.
messages.China: China supports this draft as a basis and appreciates the penholder’s efforts. Our central request is that OP8 clearly demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not merely steps toward a cessation of hostilities. We also ask that the text explicitly reject collective punishment and reaffirm the legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people within the two-State framework.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the balanced and comprehensive text and thanks Brazil for its inclusive consultations. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP8 to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, and to reinforce OP5 on access through all crossings. We can also support a reference to the prohibition of starvation as a method of warfare. Ecuador will engage constructively to avoid another veto and to ensure the Council speaks with one voice.
messages.France: France supports the draft's condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the humanitarian and two-State provisions. We believe the Council must now go further and call clearly for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in OP8, rather than only conditions for a cessation of hostilities. We also seek a short reporting deadline and stronger monitoring/deconfliction language to ensure implementation. France stands ready to work with Brazil and all Council members to finalize a text we can support.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports this draft as a basis for Council action and welcomes its balanced condemnation of attacks, its emphasis on hostages, humanitarian access and the two-State solution. We continue to believe the Council must call clearly for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and for the opening of all crossings and lifting of restrictions so that aid can reach civilians throughout Gaza. We also ask that the protection of schools and accountability for attacks on medical, humanitarian and UN personnel be explicitly reflected. We are ready to work with the penholder to preserve Council unity.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the balanced draft and its emphasis on compliance with international humanitarian law, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP8 by demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, and OP5 to explicitly require the opening of all crossings and sustained fuel supplies so that aid can reach civilians throughout Gaza. We also suggest adding 'to their homes' in OP7 to make clear that displaced persons must be able to return safely. Ghana remains committed to Council unity and will work with all delegations to secure the broadest possible support.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the balanced direction of the draft, including its condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the focus on humanitarian access and the two-State solution. To match the urgency of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, Japan asks the penholder to strengthen OP8 to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. Japan remains ready to engage constructively to secure the broadest possible Council support.
messages.Malta: Malta thanks Brazil for the balanced and carefully crafted draft and confirms its support. It reflects Malta's priorities: condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, immediate and unhindered humanitarian access, release of all hostages, and a two-State solution. Malta urges all Council members to unite behind this text and to ensure its full and immediate implementation together with resolution 2712 (2023).
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique thanks Brazil for the comprehensive draft and supports it as a basis for adoption. We would like OP8 to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, consistent with the Secretary-General's call and the position of the majority of Member States. We also ask for explicit language on lifting restrictions and opening all crossings to enable aid at scale, and for a preambular reference to the grave situation in the West Bank, including settler violence and settlements.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the humanitarian thrust of this draft and remains a co-sponsor, but the text still lacks the central demand required by the situation: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP8 accordingly and to balance the condemnation language, including with regard to indiscriminate Israeli attacks in Gaza and the root causes of the conflict. With these changes, the draft can send a meaningful signal; without them, it will not respond to the expectations of the Council and the region.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the draft and supports its core objectives: condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, rejection of forced displacement and the two-State solution. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP8 with a call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, to add respect for humanitarian principles and deconfliction mechanisms, to specify ICRC access to hostages in OP3, and to strengthen monitoring in OP11. We are ready to work constructively to find consensus.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports this text as a basis and appreciates Brazil’s efforts, but the Council cannot remain silent on a ceasefire while Gaza’s health system and humanitarian space collapse. We request that OP8 be revised to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire leading to a sustainable cessation of hostilities; this is a red line for us. We also ask that OP5 make clear that access must be immediate, sustained and at scale through all crossings, including fuel and medical supplies.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the draft’s clear condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, its affirmation of the right of self-defence and its focus on humanitarian pauses, and we can support it. We ask the penholder to add explicit condemnation of Hamas’s use of civilians as human shields and to make clear in OP8 that any sustainable cessation of hostilities must be respected by all parties and must not allow Hamas to rearm. We would also prefer OP10 to refer to a reformed and revitalized Palestinian Authority.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the balanced approach of this draft, which condemns Hamas and calls for humanitarian pauses and hostage release. However, we need an operative reaffirmation of the inherent right to self-defence under Article 51, and we must explicitly name Hamas and other terrorist groups in the condemnation and hostage-release demands. We also ask that OP8 specify that the release of all hostages must be immediate and unconditional. With these changes, we can support the text.

steps.summary: The revised text incorporates most non-ceasefire requests, strengthens humanitarian access and protection, and balances self-defence and hostage-release language. Brazil calibrates the ceasefire provision to a call rather than an immediate demand in order to retain Council viability. Broad support is expected, with possible abstentions from members seeking stronger ceasefire or root-cause language.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the revised draft as it stands. It clearly condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks and hostage-taking, reaffirms the inherent right of self-defence, and responds to the catastrophic humanitarian situation with calls for humanitarian pauses, access and a ceasefire leading to a sustainable cessation of hostilities. We urge all Council members to unite behind this balanced text.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft as a basis and welcomes the additions on collective punishment and self-determination. However, the core ceasefire language remains below what the situation requires and below the Security Council’s responsibility. We ask that OP12 be strengthened from “Calls for” to “Demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and the immediate cessation of hostilities”; with this change China can support the text.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the revised text and appreciates the incorporation of our concerns on access through all crossings and on starvation as a method of warfare. We request one final adjustment in OP12: replace 'Calls for' with 'Demands' an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, so that the Council speaks with the urgency the humanitarian catastrophe requires. Ecuador can support the draft with that change.
messages.France: France supports the revised draft and welcomes the inclusion of the 10-day reporting and monitoring options. However, given the catastrophic humanitarian situation, the Council must demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not merely call for it. We therefore request that OP12 be strengthened accordingly. France will vote in favour of the text in any case.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the incorporation of our requests on crossings, schools and accountability. However, the Council must speak with clarity and urgency on the central issue: OP12 should demand, not merely call for, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. This is essential to respond to the catastrophic situation in Gaza and to preserve the Council’s credibility. Gabon remains ready to support the text with this adjustment.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of language on crossings, fuel and the safe return of displaced persons to their homes. However, given the catastrophic humanitarian situation, we continue to believe the Council must do more than call for a ceasefire. Ghana therefore requests that OP12 be strengthened to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire leading to a sustainable cessation of hostilities, while retaining the provisions on hostage release and non-rearmament.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current text as a balanced compromise and is ready to vote in favour. We appreciate the penholder’s partial acceptance of our previous request; while we would have preferred an operative demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, we will not insist further in the interest of Council action. We urge all members to unite and adopt the text without delay.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the draft as circulated and welcomes the balanced compromise it represents. It echoes the urgent calls for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, full humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and UN personnel. Malta urges all Council members to unite and adopt the text without further delay so that resolution 2712 (2023) can be fully implemented.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique welcomes the reflected concerns on humanitarian access and the West Bank and supports the balance of the text. We continue to ask that OP12 demand, rather than merely call for, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, given the catastrophic humanitarian situation. We also ask that OP7 explicitly name Kerem Shalom so that the commitment to open all crossings is operational.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft as a co-sponsor and welcomes the inclusion of language on settlements and regional sovereignty. However, the text remains unbalanced: it still does not name Israeli indiscriminate attacks against civilians and civilian objects in Gaza, nor does it address the occupation and root causes of the conflict. We therefore ask the penholder to add the proposed references to OP3 and a new preambular paragraph, and to strengthen OP12 to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire without singling out only Hamas for rearmament.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the revised draft. It reflects our priorities: condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages with ICRC access, protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, full humanitarian access in line with humanitarian principles, and a path to an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We would have preferred a more explicit UN monitoring and verification mechanism, but we welcome the Secretary-General’s reporting and options and will not block consensus.
messages.United Arab Emirates: We welcome the inclusion of at-scale humanitarian access through crossings in OP7. However, the Council cannot merely call for a ceasefire while civilians continue to be killed in Gaza; OP12 must demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. This remains the UAE’s red line, and without it we cannot support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We welcome the inclusion of our earlier requests on human shields, rearmament and a reformed Palestinian Authority. However, the United Kingdom cannot support a call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, which risks undermining hostage negotiations and Israel's right to self-defence. We ask that OP12 be revised to call for urgent steps to create conditions for a sustainable cessation of hostilities, including through extended humanitarian pauses, while retaining the caveat that Hamas must not be allowed to rearm. With that change, we would be prepared to support the text.
messages.United States of America: We appreciate the penholder reflecting our previous requests on self-defence, condemnation of Hamas terrorism, and the immediate and unconditional release of hostages. The current OP12 remains unworkable: the United States cannot support a call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire that would leave Hamas able to repeat October 7. We ask that OP12 be revised to call for extended humanitarian pauses and to condition any sustainable cessation on hostage release and preventing Hamas from rearming. With that change, we are prepared to support the text.

steps.summary: Brazil revised OP12 to a compromise centered on urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and conditions for a sustainable cessation, addressing the US and UK red lines while retaining robust humanitarian access, protection, and accountability provisions. The text partially accommodates Russia and Mozambique on Gaza and Kerem Shalom but does not include the immediate ceasefire demand sought by China, Ecuador, Gabon, Ghana, Mozambique, Russia, or the UAE. It is expected to be adopted with 12 votes in favour and 3 abstentions.

reasons.Albania: Albania has consistently supported balanced texts that condemn Hamas, affirm Israel’s right to self-defence, and call for humanitarian access, all of which are reflected in this draft. It would likely vote in favour without requesting the floor before the vote.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil is the penholder and co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported Council action on humanitarian access, protection of civilians, hostages, and the two-State solution. Voting in favour and explaining the vote before the vote advances Brazil’s diplomatic position and efforts to build Council unity.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions and is listed as a co-sponsor; despite its red-line concern over OP12, it would vote in favour to advance civilian protection and humanitarian access.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador has consistently supported Council action on humanitarian access and protection of civilians and voted for similar texts, so it would back this draft despite its rejected amendment; it typically explains its vote after voting rather than before.
reasons.France: France supported the draft despite its unheeded request to strengthen OP12, consistent with its stated willingness to support the text in any case. It would not need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon has consistently supported ceasefire and humanitarian texts and prioritizes civilian protection, humanitarian access, and a two-State solution. Although its amendment demanding an immediate ceasefire was rejected, voting in favour aligns with its established position and maximizes pressure for aid and compliance with international law.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana has consistently supported Council action to address the humanitarian catastrophe and has voted in favour of earlier humanitarian drafts; despite the rejected OP12 amendment, the overall text aligns with its priorities, and a yes vote advances protection, aid, and ceasefire momentum.
reasons.Japan: Japan’s established position supports a balanced Council response condemning Hamas, demanding hostage release and humanitarian access, while recognizing self-defence and international law; this draft aligns with those priorities and with Japan’s prior votes in favour of humanitarian resolutions.
reasons.Malta: Malta co-sponsored the draft and supported it throughout negotiations, consistent with its focus on humanitarian access, civilian protection and a two-State solution. No pre-vote explanation was required before casting an affirmative vote.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique has consistently supported ceasefire and humanitarian texts; despite the unmet request to strengthen OP12, this balanced draft aligns with its prior support for resolution 2712 and its calls for civilian protection and humanitarian access. Speaking before the vote explains support while pressing for stronger action.
reasons.Russian Federation: As a co-sponsor and consistent advocate of a ceasefire, Russia supports the draft despite incomplete amendments; its support_with_changes position and earlier votes indicate a yes vote.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland supported the draft in negotiations and its provisions align with Swiss priorities on international humanitarian law, humanitarian access, hostage release, and civilian protection. As in prior votes, Switzerland would likely explain its vote after the vote rather than before.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE is a co-sponsor and has consistently supported humanitarian resolutions that advance aid and civilian protection, even when they fall short of an explicit immediate ceasefire. Voting in favour aligns with its record of supporting compromises like resolution 2712 and its active role in shaping this text.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The final draft incorporates the UK’s red-line change to OP12 and includes key UK priorities: explicit condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, reaffirmation of Israel’s right to self-defence, and demands for hostage release and humanitarian access. Given this balanced text, the UK would vote in favour.
reasons.United States of America: The United States secured its red-line change to OP12, removing an immediate ceasefire call and conditioning any sustainable cessation on hostage release and preventing Hamas from rearming. The draft now condemns Hamas, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence, and calls for humanitarian pauses, making it consistent with US policy and acceptable to support.

before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which it has tabled with broad cross-regional co-sponsorship. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires this Council to act with urgency, responsibility and unity. The text builds on resolution 2712 (2023), condemns the heinous Hamas attacks of 7 October and the taking of hostages, and rejects indiscriminate attacks and collective punishment of civilians. It demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and humanitarian and medical personnel, and compliance with international humanitarian law. It also addresses the dangerous regional dimension and reaffirms the two-State solution and the unity of Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Brazil calls on all Council members to support this balanced and necessary text.
before.Gabon: Gabon will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Brazil and all co-sponsors for their efforts to bring the Council together in the face of an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe. My delegation regrets that our proposal to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire was not retained, as the gravity of the situation requires the Council to speak with the utmost clarity. Nevertheless, this text contains essential provisions on the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, the release of hostages, the protection of medical and United Nations personnel and facilities, and the rejection of forced displacement. Gabon cannot turn its back on these commitments. We call on all parties to comply with international humanitarian law and to allow full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in Gaza, especially children. The Council must act to save lives and to support a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution. Gabon will vote in favour.
before.Ghana: Ghana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the Council cannot remain silent while civilians in Gaza face a catastrophic humanitarian situation, and because the text demands humanitarian access, the release of hostages and respect for international humanitarian law. We regret that our proposed amendment to OP12, which would have demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, was not accepted; nevertheless, we see this text as an important step that the Council must not fail to adopt.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Brazil and the co-sponsors for their inclusive efforts to produce a balanced text at a time when the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic and the Council must act. Japan strongly condemns the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups and demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, all parties must comply with international humanitarian law, protect civilians and humanitarian and medical personnel and facilities, and allow full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including through urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors. Japan also reaffirms Israel’s inherent right to self-defence, which must be exercised in full compliance with international law, rejects forced displacement, and reiterates its unwavering support for the two-State solution and the illegality of Israeli settlement activities. We call on all parties to engage constructively to create the conditions for a sustainable cessation of hostilities and a just and lasting peace.
before.Mozambique: Mr. President, Mozambique thanks the sponsors for their efforts to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We remain gravely concerned by the continuing loss of civilian life, especially children, and by the worsening humanitarian emergency. While we would have preferred that the Council demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, as we proposed, we recognize the urgent need for the Council to act and to reinforce the implementation of resolution 2712 (2023). Mozambique will therefore vote in favour, and calls on all parties to protect civilians, release all hostages immediately and unconditionally, allow full humanitarian access, and work towards a just and lasting two-State solution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of this draft. We have consistently called for a cessation of hostilities, unhindered humanitarian access and the release of all hostages, and we condemn all attacks against civilians, including the terrorist attacks of 7 October. We regret that not all our proposals were fully taken into account, especially the need to clearly condemn indiscriminate Israeli attacks and to address the root causes, including illegal settlement activities and the occupation. Nevertheless, this draft contains important elements and sends a necessary signal that the Council must act to stop the bloodshed and the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. We call on all members to support it.
before.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands that this Council act without further delay. The United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this resolution. It is not the text we had hoped for—we continue to believe that an immediate humanitarian ceasefire is the only way to end the suffering—but it contains essential provisions to scale up humanitarian access, protect civilians, secure the release of hostages, reject forced displacement, and create conditions for a sustainable cessation of hostilities. We call for its full and immediate implementation. The Council must not remain silent while civilians are killed and hospitals collapse. We will continue to press for an immediate ceasefire and for a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution. Thank you.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom has consistently called for a balanced text that condemns Hamas’s appalling terrorist attacks, reaffirms Israel’s inherent right to self-defence in accordance with international law, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and addresses the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We welcome that this draft now does exactly that. It also calls for urgent steps to create the conditions for a sustainable cessation of hostilities through extended humanitarian pauses, and makes clear that any sustainable cessation must not allow Hamas to rearm or replenish its military capabilities. We support the demands for full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and the rejection of forced displacement. The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution and calls on all parties to implement it fully and immediately.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. We thank Brazil and the co-sponsors for their efforts to bring the Council together at a moment when the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic and the credibility of this Council is at stake.

This resolution sends a clear and necessary message. It condemns the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and insists on the protection of civilians and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. Albania reiterates its full support for Israel’s inherent right to self-defence, in accordance with international law, and stresses that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack.

We call for the full and immediate implementation of this resolution and of resolution 2712 (2023). Humanitarian pauses and corridors must be respected, humanitarian personnel and United Nations facilities must be protected, and aid must reach all civilians in need, including in northern Gaza. We also recall the need to reject forced displacement and to work towards a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders.

Albania will continue to support every effort aimed at ending the suffering of civilians, securing the release of hostages and preventing a wider regional escalation. Thank you.
after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution just adopted. As the penholder, we thank all members of the Council for their constructive engagement and the broad cross-regional group of co-sponsors for their support. Today the Council has spoken with one voice at a moment when civilians in Gaza are facing an unacceptable humanitarian catastrophe. That unity must now be translated into concrete action on the ground.

Brazil stresses that this resolution demands the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2712 (2023), the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors throughout Gaza, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including through all available crossings. It demands the protection of civilians, medical and humanitarian personnel, United Nations facilities and critical civilian infrastructure, and it rejects forced displacement and the use of starvation as a method of warfare. These are not optional commitments; they are obligations under international humanitarian law.

Brazil remains gravely concerned by the regional dimension of the conflict and calls on all actors to exercise maximum restraint. We reiterate our condemnation of the heinous attacks by Hamas on 7 October and of all attacks against civilians. The only path to a just and lasting peace is the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, and with Gaza reunited with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

Brazil will continue to work with the Secretary-General, Council members and regional partners to ensure that this resolution is implemented without delay. The Council must remain seized of the matter and be ready to act again if the situation on the ground does not improve.

Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of this resolution and was a co-sponsor. We thank Brazil and all co-sponsors for their efforts to seek the broadest consensus within the Council. In the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the growing risk of regional escalation, the Council could not remain silent. The adoption of this resolution demonstrates that the Council can and must shoulder its responsibility.

China has consistently urged an immediate ceasefire and cessation of hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Gaza. We condemn all attacks against civilians and civilian objects, including the heinous attacks of 7 October. International humanitarian law must be observed by all parties. The protection of civilians, medical personnel, United Nations facilities and humanitarian workers must be ensured. The right to self-defence cannot be used as a pretext for indiscriminate attacks or collective punishment of the Palestinian people.

The key now is full and immediate implementation. The Council must follow up on the implementation of this resolution and resolution 2712 (2023), and ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches those in need at scale and without obstruction. China will continue to work with Council members and the international community to this end.

The Palestinian question remains the core of the Middle East issue. The only way to achieve lasting peace and security is to return to the two-State solution, establish an independent State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital, and ensure the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people. The Security Council must remain seized of the matter and continue to play its role in promoting a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement.

Thank you.
after.Ecuador:
Mr. President,

Ecuador voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We welcome the unity of the Council at a moment when civilians in Gaza are enduring an intolerable humanitarian catastrophe. We thank Brazil and all co-sponsors for their efforts to produce a text that reflects the urgency of the situation and the obligations of all parties under international law.

We condemn all attacks against civilians, including the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas and other groups on 7 October, and the taking of hostages. The immediate and unconditional release of all hostages remains essential. At the same time, all parties must comply with international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack. The inherent right to self-defence does not exempt any State from those obligations. We reiterate our grave concern at the suffering of children, women, medical personnel and humanitarian workers, and we reject any forced displacement of the civilian population.

The Council must now insist on the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2712 (2023) and of the resolution just adopted. That means urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors, full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza, the protection of hospitals, United Nations premises and humanitarian personnel, and the scaling-up of assistance without preconditions. We call on all parties to facilitate the delivery of food, water, fuel, medicine and emergency repairs and to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.

Ecuador remains convinced that there can be no military solution to this conflict. We reaffirm our support for a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, and with Gaza reunited with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. The Council must remain seized of this matter and must not remain silent in the face of threats to international peace and security. Thank you.
after.France:
Thank you, Mr. President. France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. In the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the Council has finally spoken with one voice. This text responds to the gravity of the moment: it condemns the terrorist attacks committed by Hamas on 7 October, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and calls for full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. Those demands must now be implemented without delay.

France recalls Israel’s right to defend itself and its legitimate security concerns. At the same time, all parties must comply strictly with international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution, and must protect civilians, especially children, as well as medical personnel, United Nations premises and humanitarian workers. The humanitarian pauses provided for in this resolution must be extended, respected by all parties and translated into a lasting cessation of hostilities. France will continue to work actively to that end.

France also remains gravely concerned by the violence in the West Bank and by settlement activities, which undermine the prospect of a two-State solution. The region must not be allowed to slide into further escalation. France reaffirms its commitment to a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, with Gaza reunited with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. France will continue to shoulder its responsibilities and calls on all parties to comply fully with this resolution and with their obligations under international law.
after.Malta:
Mr. President,

Malta voted in favour of this resolution, which we were honoured to co-sponsor. We welcome the Council’s unity at a moment when civilians in Gaza are enduring a humanitarian catastrophe. We thank Brazil and all co-sponsors for their inclusive efforts to produce a balanced and action-oriented text.

Malta unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October, as well as all attacks against civilians. We reiterate our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and for the International Committee of the Red Cross to be granted immediate access to them.

All parties must comply with international humanitarian law. Israel has the inherent right to self-defence, which must be exercised in full conformity with international law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack. Civilians, especially children, and medical and humanitarian personnel, hospitals, schools and United Nations facilities must be protected. The reports of attacks on hospitals, ambulances and UN shelters are deeply alarming and must be investigated, with accountability for violations.

The true test of this resolution is its full and immediate implementation, together with resolution 2712 (2023). Malta calls for full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza, including through all available crossings and without preconditions; for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors respected by all parties; for the scaling-up of life-saving assistance; and for the safe return of displaced persons, in rejection of forced displacement. We also remain gravely concerned by violence against Palestinian civilians in the West Bank, including by extremist settlers, and by illegal settlement expansion, and we call for accountability and respect for international law.

The humanitarian response cannot substitute for a political horizon. Malta reaffirms its support for a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, with Gaza reunited with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Malta will remain seized of this matter and stands ready to work with all Council members to ensure that today’s unity is translated into real protection and relief for civilians. Thank you.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland voted in favour of the resolution just adopted and welcomes its unanimous adoption. We thank Brazil and all co-sponsors for their efforts to bridge positions at a moment of extreme urgency. The value of the Council speaking with one voice will be measured by whether it now changes the reality on the ground.

Switzerland unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas and other groups on 7 October and the taking of hostages. We reiterate our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and for the International Committee of the Red Cross to be granted immediate access to them. We condemn all attacks against civilians and civilian objects and all violations of international humanitarian law. Israel’s legitimate right to self-defence must be exercised in full respect of international law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack.

The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza is intolerable. Switzerland calls for the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2712 (2023) and of the resolution just adopted. Urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors must be respected by all parties. Humanitarian assistance must reach civilians throughout Gaza, including in the north, rapidly, safely and unhindered, through all available crossings and without preconditions. Medical and humanitarian personnel, United Nations facilities and critical civilian infrastructure must be protected. We reject forced displacement and stress the need to create conditions for the safe return of displaced persons.

Switzerland would have preferred the Council to go further, including by demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. Nevertheless, we voted in favour because this text contains essential obligations that must now be implemented without delay. We remain deeply concerned by the risk of regional escalation and call on all States and actors to exercise maximum restraint and avoid any action that could widen the conflict.

The only path to a just and lasting peace remains a negotiated two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, and with Gaza reunited with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Switzerland will continue to support every effort to alleviate suffering, protect civilians and restore a political horizon.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution and thanks Brazil and all co-sponsors for their efforts to produce a balanced text. We voted in favour because this Council has spoken with clarity on the terrorist attacks by Hamas of 7 October, on the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, on Israel’s inherent right to self-defence in accordance with international law, and on the urgent need for expanded humanitarian access and extended humanitarian pauses. These are not competing imperatives; they are mutually reinforcing obligations that all parties must respect.

The humanitarian situation in Gaza is dire, and too many civilians, including children, have lost their lives. Palestinian civilians are not Hamas. The United States has worked intensively with Israel, Egypt, Qatar, the United Nations and other partners to increase the flow of food, water, medicine, fuel and other assistance into Gaza and to secure the release of hostages. We will continue that work. This resolution must now be implemented in full: hostages released; humanitarian access scaled up and sustained throughout Gaza; civilians protected; humanitarian and medical personnel and facilities safeguarded; and deconfliction mechanisms made to work.

The United States remains committed to Israel’s security and to the protection of civilians in accordance with international humanitarian law. We also remain committed to a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security, and with Gaza reunited with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. The Council must remain engaged and ensure that the words of this resolution are translated into action on the ground. Thank you.
